solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Emu wants to transform, becoming this?

definitions.text: Emu wants to transform, becoming this?

indicators.note: Transforming something changes its form, so the letters named get rebuilt in a new order.

parts.note: eight letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A flightless Australian bird dreams of becoming a different bird altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an emu that rebuilds itself into another bird becomes the swan its own letters spell.
explanation.definitionFit: The mute swan is the common white swan of Britain, one bird an emu could wish to turn into.

clue.text: Spooner's guided writer in selection of music

indicators.note: The Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words, so the two things clued here trade their fronts.

parts.note: guided is LED, and it takes the M from the next word
the writer is ME, the setter speaking of himself, and it takes the L in exchange

explanation.surface: Someone being steered through a set of tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'led me' and swap the opening sounds to hear 'med-lee'; the second half is then respelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley is a run of tunes played one after another, a selection strung together.

clue.text: Skill shown by driver with any luck

parts.note: a deft touch is skill
a driver is a wood, the golf club for long shots

explanation.surface: A golfer's skill off the tee, helped by a bit of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: "Driver" wants to be a motorist; it is the golf club, which is one of the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: People say 'touch wood' when hoping good luck holds, much as they say 'with any luck'.

clue.text: Short sailor all but unsuitable for naval battle

indicators.note: A word cut short loses its end, so SALT drops its last letter.
All but a word is the whole of it except the last letter.

parts.note: SALT, an old sailor, without its last letter
AMISS, out of place, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A small sailor is judged unfit to fight at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Salamis, 480 BC, is where the Greek fleet beat the Persians.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Salamis was fought between ships off an island near Athens, so it is a naval battle.

clue.text: Unaltered having adopted parking orbit position

parts.note: left as is, unchanged
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A car park left just as it was.
explanation.walkthrough: The P goes in after the first letter of AS IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An apsis is either point of an orbit nearest to or farthest from the body being circled.

clue.text: Gossip good when appropriate

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
as in 'as I left', meaning when
to bag something is to take it for yourself

explanation.surface: Advice that gossip is fine when the moment suits.
explanation.walkthrough: "Appropriate" looks like an adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb, to seize, which is BAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is someone who talks endlessly, and a gossip is one such chatterer.

clue.text: Professional called to account in Listener

definitions.meaning: the accountant called in to check the books

explanation.surface: An expert summoned to explain himself before a listening audience.
explanation.walkthrough: "Called to account" reads as being made to answer for something; here it is being called in to the accounts. The Listener is also the name of a famous crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor inspects accounts for a living, and also, in the older sense, is simply one who hears.

clue.text: Times perhaps writing about romantic figure

parts.note: three by four is three times four
writing is one of the three Rs
a talk on something is about it

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper running a piece on a romantic lead.
explanation.walkthrough: "Times" looks like this very newspaper; it is the multiplication sign read as BY. The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron was a leading poet of the Romantic movement and a famously romantic figure.

clue.text: Behave as faithful sweethearts? So get day fixed

indicators.note: Something fixed has been rearranged into working order, so the letters get put into a new one.

parts.note: eight letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A couple told to name the date for their wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as fixing a wedding day, which suits the definition nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: To go steady is to date one person exclusively, as faithful sweethearts do.

clue.text: Judge an AA Milne character shunning love in classic

indicators.note: To shun something is to keep it out, so the O leaves the name.

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
taken as printed
EEYORE, the gloomy donkey, without O, love being zero in tennis

explanation.surface: A judge assesses a Winnie-the-Pooh character who has given up on love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O because a score of nil in tennis is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre, Charlotte Brontë's novel of 1847, is a classic of English literature.

clue.text: Rules unfairly applied in tennis match, restricting quality

parts.note: a tennis match with two players on each side
a high standard is high quality

explanation.surface: A tennis umpire bends the rules while cutting the standard of play.
explanation.walkthrough: STANDARD sits inside DOUBLES, just before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Double standards are principles applied to some people but not others, which is to say rules unfairly applied.

clue.text: Unearths former partner of philosopher

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
HUME'S, belonging to David Hume, the Scottish philosopher

explanation.surface: Someone digs up the ex-wife of a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of HUME'S is dropped, as in all grid entries.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig out of the ground, the literal sense of unearth.

clue.text: Medical speciality doubled European understanding

indicators.note: Doubling a thing writes it twice.

parts.note: ear, nose and throat
the same three letters again
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European grasp of a medical specialism, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is the hospital department for ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: What troubles flesh or bay's rear?

definitions.text: What troubles flesh or bay's rear?

indicators.note: Troubling something stirs it up, so the letters of 'flesh or' get disturbed into a new order.

parts.note: seven letters in a new order

indicators.note: The rear of a word is its last letter.

parts.note: the last letter of bay

explanation.surface: A riddle about what bothers skin or the hindquarters of a bay horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a bay is a reddish-brown horse, and a horsefly bites flesh and rumps alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The horsefly is a biting fly that plagues horses, so it is what troubles a bay's rear.

clue.text: Jet following unseats Mike in spectacular rise

indicators.note: Unseating a rider throws him off, so the M is thrown out of MOUNTAIN.

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in 'p. 12 f.'
MOUNTAIN, a spectacular rise, without M, which is Mike in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An aircraft chasing someone throws a pilot off during a dramatic climb.
explanation.walkthrough: "Jet" looks like a plane; it is a spout of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountain is a jet of water thrown into the air.

clue.text: Restrained Republican newspaper commentary

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
an op-ed is an opinion piece opposite the editorial page

explanation.surface: A newspaper column by a Republican that holds back.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen of OP-ED drops out in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something roped has been tied up, which is to say restrained.

clue.text: Flower power on the up must embrace hard facts

indicators.note: In a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards.
Embracing something wraps arms round it.

parts.note: a spring flower
P is the physics symbol for power
H is the pencil grade for hard

explanation.surface: Flower power is on the rise but must face hard truths.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed ANEMONE and P give PENOMENA, and H goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are things observed to happen, facts of experience.

clue.text: Sister to volatile pre-Raphaelite founder

indicators.note: Something volatile is unstable, liable to break apart, so the letters shift into a new order.

parts.note: eight letters taken as printed

explanation.surface: A temperamental sister of one of the painters who began the Pre-Raphaelite movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits: Christina Rossetti, the poet, was the sister of Dante Gabriel Rossetti, a founder of the Brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti co-founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood in 1848.

clue.text: Serviceman giving up coat for senior citizen

indicators.note: A word's coat is its outer layer, its first and last letters, and giving it up leaves the inside.

parts.note: SOLDIER without its S and R

explanation.surface: A soldier trades in his coat for an older person.
explanation.walkthrough: "Coat" looks like a uniform garment; it is the outer letters of SOLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal word for an old person, a senior citizen.

clue.text: British earl returned billions reportedly secured in current recession

indicators.note: What is returned goes back, so the two letters come in reverse order.

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
E is the abbreviation for earl
B is the abbreviation for billions

indicators.note: A report is what you hear said, so the word is the one that sounds the same.

parts.note: secured is TIED, which sounds like TIDE

explanation.surface: A British nobleman brings his billions home during an economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: "Recession" wants the economy; here it is water receding, and the current is the tidal one.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb tide is the outgoing tide, a current as the sea recedes.

clue.text: Regularly humbled rogue seeks illustrious techie

indicators.note: Taking letters regularly means every other one, here the second, fourth, sixth and so on.

parts.note: hUmBlEd RoGuE, every second letter
sEeKs, continuing the same rhythm

explanation.surface: A rogue brought low goes looking for a famous computer whizz.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhythm runs straight across all three words, so 'seeks' is fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ubergeek is a geek of the highest order, a techie of great standing.

clue.text: Travel north: see the sights of coastal city in boat

parts.note: to go is to travel
N is the abbreviation for north
to 'do' Paris is to tour it
LA is Los Angeles, on the Pacific coast

explanation.surface: A tourist heads north to take in a seaside city by water.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Venice, where the gondola belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is the long flat-bottomed boat rowed on the canals of Venice.

clue.text: Pascal, detective keeping your old documents

parts.note: Pa is the symbol for the pascal, the unit of pressure

indicators.note: What keeps something holds it.

parts.note: a PI is a private investigator
YR is the abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: A detective named Pascal hangs on to someone's ancient papers.
explanation.walkthrough: "Pascal" looks like a first name; it is the unit of pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyri are ancient manuscripts written on papyrus, old documents indeed.

clue.text: Superseded instrument in fire ship from the east

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them

indicators.note: In an across entry, reading from the east means right to left, so the letters run backwards.

parts.note: a tub is a slow old ship

explanation.surface: An old instrument aboard a burning ship coming in from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fire ship" reads as one thing, a burning vessel sent against an enemy fleet; the two words are separate parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut was the early trombone, superseded by the modern instrument.

clue.text: Further attempt to support Conservative doctrine

indicators.note: In a down entry, a support sits underneath.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a redo is another go

explanation.surface: A second attempt to back Conservative policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Conservatives are one of Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs, a doctrine one lives by.

clue.text: She released evil men held inside police car

indicators.note: What is held inside something sits within it.

parts.note: a panda car is a British police patrol car
other ranks, the soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An arrest story: a woman freed some wicked men locked in a squad car.
explanation.walkthrough: "Evil men" wants to be one phrase; "evil" belongs to the definition and "men" alone gives OR.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pandora opened the jar that let every evil loose into the world.

clue.text: Religious work that is introduced to school organisation

indicators.note: What is introduced goes into something.

parts.note: Parent-Teacher Association
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A piece of religious study brought to a school society.
explanation.walkthrough: "Work" looks like effort; here it is a work of art. The PTA is the body of parents and teachers that raises funds for a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of Mary holding the dead Christ, Michelangelo's being the best known.

clue.text: Deceived with myth on broadcast about one medieval work

indicators.note: Broadcasting scatters something far and wide, so the letters are thrown into a new order.
About means round, so the rearranged letters go round the I.

parts.note: taken as printed
taken as printed
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone taken in by a myth that was broadcast about a medieval book.
explanation.walkthrough: "With" only joins the two lots of fodder, and the I lands inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's Divine Comedy, written in the early 1300s, is the great medieval Italian poem.

clue.text: Two or three brought into Irish compound

indicators.note: What is brought into something ends up inside it.

parts.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish
a few, an unspecified small number

explanation.surface: A couple of things added to an Irish mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: "Compound" looks like a word for mixture in the surface; it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An isomer is a chemical compound with the same atoms as another arranged differently.

clue.text: Spy husband in Paris securing cover for each revolutionary

indicators.note: Securing something holds it fast.
A revolution turns something round.

parts.note: mari is French for husband
a hat covers the head
as in 'a pound a head'

explanation.surface: A husband in Paris covers for a rebel who is spying.
explanation.walkthrough: "Revolutionary" wants to be a noun, a rebel in the surface; it is the instruction to turn round the two parts before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mata Hari was the Dutch dancer shot as a German spy in 1917.
